section_summary: The section opens with a Treasury Bureau of Narcotics letter of 7 August 1947 forwarding Japanese and Korean narcotics reports to the State Department for the Permanent Central Opium Board. It contains the Second Quarter 1947 statistical forms for Japan (all nil) and Korea (imports from US Army stocks). It also holds the SCAP reply on Japan's narcotics laws, with the Japanese Narcotic Control Regulation (Ministry of Welfare Ordinance No. 25 and No. 27, 19 June 1946). The last part is South Korea's questionnaire answers with USAMGIK Ordinance 119 (1946) and Public Health Order No. 3 (1947), which continues past page 42.

subfiles.about: Forwards statistical forms and questionnaire replies from Japan and Korea for transmission to the Permanent Central Opium Board.
subfiles.from: Will S. Wood, Acting Commissioner of Narcotics
subfiles.summary: Enclosures: Q2 1947 Form A(GL) for Japan and Korea, and their replies to UN questionnaires E/CN.7/64 and E/CN.7/63.
subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Japan and Korea narcotics reports to State Department
subfiles.to: George H. Morlock, Department of State

subfiles.about: Quarterly narcotics import and export statistics for Japan, signed by SCAP.
subfiles.from: Crawford F. Sams, SCAP Public Health and Welfare Section
subfiles.summary: Printed Geneva form with instructions, notes and equivalence table; all import and export entries are nil for Japan.
subfiles.title: Statistical Form A(GL) Second Quarter 1947 - Japan

subfiles.about: Quarterly narcotics statistics for South Korea showing imports from US Army stocks and the Civilian Supply program.
subfiles.from: Y. S. Lee, Director, Department of Public Health and Welfare, Korea
subfiles.summary: Korea reports imports of medicinal opium, ethylmorphine, cocaine and codeine received from US Army stocks and civilian supply, with no exports. Remarks explain the quantities.
subfiles.title: Statistical Form A(GL) Second Quarter 1947 - Korea

subfiles.about: Answers for Japan to UN questionnaire E/CN.7/64 citing the relevant Narcotic Control Regulations.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, SCAP (R. G. Hersey, for the Supreme Commander)
subfiles.summary: Replies question by question on possession, addiction, registration of addicts, treatment by physicians and licensing, quoting Articles of the Narcotic Control Regulations. Notes a law on commitment of addicts is expected, modelled on the US Uniform State Laws.
subfiles.title: SCAP reply to questionnaire on legal and practical standpoint on drug addiction

subfiles.about: Official Gazette English edition text of the Narcotic Control Regulation and the Ordinance amending the Pharmacopoeia list.
subfiles.summary: Defines narcotics and marihuana and classes of narcotic dealers. It sets licensing, registration tax, reporting, record-keeping, inspection and penalties (Arts. 1-64). Ordinance No. 27 removes cocaine, codeine, morphine hydrochloride and opium tincture from the standing medicines list.
subfiles.title: Japanese Narcotic Control Regulation, Ministry of Welfare Ordinance Nos. 25 and 27

subfiles.about: Korean answers to the UN questionnaire on legal and practical standpoint on drug addiction.
subfiles.from: Department of Public Health and Welfare, South Korean Interim Government
subfiles.summary: Non-medical use is not punishable as such, and addiction is undefined in law. Practitioners must report addicts, no institutional treatment exists yet but a 400-bed hospital is planned, and doctors may not treat addiction with narcotics. Stock limits apply.
subfiles.title: South Korea answers to questionnaire on drug addiction

subfiles.about: Ordinance controlling narcotic drugs in Korea south of the 38th parallel.
subfiles.from: Archer L. Lerch, Military Governor in Korea
subfiles.summary: Transfers the Narcotics Control Section to the Department of Public Health and Welfare and defines narcotic drugs. It prohibits opium poppy, marihuana, heroin and opium smoking, requires licences for narcotic transactions, and sets licence conditions, revocation and seizure. Penalties are set by Military Occupation Courts.
subfiles.title: USAMGIK Ordinance No. 119, Narcotics Control

subfiles.about: Implements Ordinance 119 with rules on licence classes, applications, fees and licence lapse; the text continues beyond page 42.
subfiles.from: Department of Public Health and Welfare, USAMGIK
subfiles.summary: Prohibits unlicensed narcotic transactions and defines licence types: manufacturer, repackager, wholesaler, pharmacist, practitioner, research and exempt preparations. It sets out application contents, fees in won, renewal, lapse and transfer rules. Practitioners must report addicts.
subfiles.title: USAMGIK Public Health Department Order No. 3, Narcotics Regulation
